title: The jazz clubs that kept jazz alive in New Orleans
summary: He credits the local jazz clubs with keeping the music alive, recalling free concerts his group played for them and his honorary memberships.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Have you found like in the past fifteen years that jazz is being appreciated, like a lot more people are listening to?

Well yeah. What would happen, I think the jazz club had a whole lot to do with keeping it alive. Because I used to do a whole lot of it. I don't know if you know, Harry Schuchon and Doc Schuchon. They're French. Well there was Helen Ault and all of them. I don't know if you know her. You don't know anything about jazz at all then. You don't know them because they don't want to keep the jazz club. Still it's not as live as it should be now. But they kept it and we used to, our group, used to do a lot of gratties for them. We'd play their concerts and things you know. It was free. They'd get places at the hotels and buy drinks and stuff like that. They didn't make any money. And once in a while now they give concerts now. But I think by the jazz club that kept the things sort of alive and they'd get their people to give their services, musicians. And I really believe that sort of helped them. Well they have a whole lot of jazz clubs all open now. And I'm an honorary member to two or three of them. I was a financial member here but I didn't pay my dues last year.
